ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) under FATF Recommendation 12 and the Gibraltar AML/CFT Supervisor's rules. Automated sanctions screening against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, HM Treasury Consolidated List, EU consolidated sanctions, and the Gibraltar sanctions list. Additional adverse media checks, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring with periodic re-screening at least every 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry online portal (Companies House Gibraltar eServices)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English using Roman script; no statutory transliteration is required in Gibraltar. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' and cannot create a link to the Crown, Government, or the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission without prior written consent. A foreign company registering in Gibraltar must use its exact corporate name from its home jurisdiction unless that name is unavailable or contrary to Gibraltar law.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of a rejection notice from the Companies Registry, the applicant may request written reasons. A formal appeal must be lodged with the Registrar within 21 days, stating the proposed name and the technical grounds for eligibility. If the Registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may, within 30 days, apply for judicial review before the Supreme Court of Gibraltar under Order 53 of the Supreme Court Rules. Alternatively, the applicant may promptly reserve an alternative cleared name. Any name containing tokens that prompted the rejection may not be re-submitted without a consent letter from the relevant Gibraltar ministry or the Financial Services Commission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not generally permissible for regulated equity crowdfunding portal operations in Gibraltar; the Financial Services Commission requires a physical registered office in Gibraltar and a local principal place of business where board oversight, compliance, and AML functions are effectively conducted. A virtual address may only serve as a supplementary correspondence address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High probability of an unannounced on-site inspection, estimated at 80% within the first 12 months of licensing, given the high-risk AML/CFT categorisation of crowdfunding intermediaries and the Financial Services Commission supervisory cycle.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Bermuda Companies Act 1981, ss. 4, 10, 18, 39 and 56 (incorporation, memorandum, exempted company status, registered office and statutory registers); Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, Pt. XX (registration of external companies); Gibraltar Financial Services (Investment Services) Act 2019 and the GFSC Crowdfunding Platform Rules (regulatory licensing)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Corporate Registry, Hamilton (primary incorporation); Gibraltar Registrar of Companies, GFSC Registry, Gibraltar (external company registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an Exempted Company and Memorandum of Association issued as the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation; Form E – Application for Registration as an External Company in Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Bermuda Exempted Company under the Companies Act 1981; however, the GFSC equity crowdfunding licence requires minimum safeguarding capital of USD 50,000 (or EUR 50,000 equivalent) to be deposited in a segregated client-money escrow account at a GFSC-authorised Gibraltar bank before commencement of crowdfunding operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED that the Company accepts the subscription for 1,000 ordinary shares at US$1.00 each and allots such shares to the initial subscriber named in the Memorandum of Association upon full payment of the subscription consideration.
RESOLVED that the registered office be established at the address approved by the Directors, and that the Notice of Registered Office be filed with the Registrar.
RESOLVED that the persons named in the Consent and Appointment Forms be appointed as first Directors and Company Secretary, to hold office until the first Annual General Meeting or until successors are duly elected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (Corporate Registry, Hamilton) and Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (name-check window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a formal name search in the Bermuda register and reserve the proposed company name through a licensed Bermuda corporate service provider; the reservation remains valid for 90 days. Simultaneously submit a name availability query to the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies to verify that the same name can be registered as an external company in Gibraltar. Confirm the name does not contain prohibited terms such as 'bank', 'trust', 'insurance' or 'royal' unless the relevant GFSC authorisation is appended.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of intended subscribers
Beneficial ownership particulars for the ultimate owners
Letter of instruction from the formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on grounds of similarity or as objectionable, file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar within 14 days of refusal, or immediately file one of the pre-reserved alternative names without additional scrutiny fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Apostille of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Bermuda corporate service provider and an admitted Bermuda notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage the licensed formation agent to prepare the Memorandum of Association and Bye-laws of the exempted company in compliance with Bermuda Companies Act 1981 ss. 10-18. Ensure the objects clause permits regulated crowdfunding intermediary activities and the non-resident exempted declaration is included. Arrange execution of the documents by the subscriber in counterpart, have the signatures notarized, and obtain an apostille certificate under the Hague Convention to enable later filing in Gibraltar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar identifies defective or ultra vires clauses, the corporate service provider revises the constitution, obtains re-execution by the subscriber, and re-presents the notarized package; the apostille is re-issued within 48 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (Corporate Registry, Hamilton)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Application for Incorporation of an Exempted Company together with the Memorandum and Bye-laws, registered office consent, and consent of the first directors, through the licensed formation agent. Pay the official state filing fee of USD 1,730. Upon complete scrutiny, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Thereafter the agent prints the share certificates, statutory registers, and the company seal.
required_dossiers: Consent of first directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a requisition letter, the agent must file a formal response with corrected documents within 21 days; a stale requisition is cured by re-filing the full package plus a reactivation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Companies House, GFSC Supervised Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the registered external company application with the Gibraltar Registrar using the apostilled Bermuda certificate, apostilled constitutional documents, a certified list of directors and secretary, and a Gibraltar registered office address. Appoint a Gibraltar-resident representative for service of process and pay the prescribed registration fee. Obtain the Gibraltar Certificate of External Registration and the Gibraltar company registration number.
required_dossiers: Certified list of directors and company secretary
Power of attorney appointing Gibraltar representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is objected due to translation, apostille, or missing consent, file the corrected documentation within 10 business days; late-day corrections are accepted with a prescribed rectification fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Equity Crowdfunding Platform Licence Application to GFSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) – Licensing and Enforcement Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the licence application under the Financial Services (Investment Services) Act 2019, presenting the equity crowdfunding business model, the AML/CFT programme, the client-money safeguarding and escrow arrangement, the outsourcing and IT security plan, and the fit-and-proper file for each director, shareholder, and beneficial owner. Pay the application fee and respond to any GFSC clarification. The Commission assesses against the Crowdfunding Platform Rules and the Gibraltar capital adequacy requirements.
required_dossiers: Business plan and five-year financial projections
Fit-and-proper declarations, police and bankruptcy certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the GFSC issues a 'notice of intention to refuse', the applicant may file representations and request an oral hearing before the GFSC within 10 business days; alternatively, resubmit after amending the governance framework, capital position, or AML controls.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Safeguarding Escrow, Occupational Clearance, and Commencement Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GFSC-authorised Gibraltar bank (escrow agent) and Gibraltar Health and Safety Inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a segregated client-money escrow account at an authorised bank and execute the escrow agreement in the form approved by the GFSC; deposit the minimum safeguarding capital of USD 50,000. Appoint the AML Compliance Officer and Money Laundering Reporting Officer. Obtain fire safety certification and occupational health clearance for the operational premises, then file the commencement of business notice and notify the GFSC of the live platform address.
required_dossiers: Escrow account opening forms and bank KYC pack
AML Compliance Officer consent and certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced KYC conditions, submit the ultimate-beneficial-owner enhanced due-diligence pack and an attestation of source of funds; if the fire or occupational inspection reveals non-compliance, remedy the premises and obtain a re-inspection within 15 working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) – Licensing and Enforcement Division; premises oversight coordinated with the Gibraltar Building Control Office and the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Gibraltar Equity Crowdfunding Operator Licence (authorisation under the Financial Services (Investment Services) Act 2019, with GFSC-regulated conduct of business, client-money safeguarding and AML/CFT permissions)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar (EIA Unit)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-level screening (Category C) – the crowdfunding portal is an office-based digital intermediary; a full EIA Report is not required as there is no manufacturing, land remediation, or point-source discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission bands are applicable. The operator must nevertheless comply with the Gibraltar Waste and Recycling Regulations for segregated disposal of WEEE and ICT hardware, use data hosting certified to ISO 14001 or equivalent, and if on-site generators or cooling are installed, comply with the Gibraltar Air Pollution Control limits (PM10, NOx) for combustion plant below 1 MWth.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and annual inspection by the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service; building control and structural load approval under the Gibraltar Building Regulations for the office premises; workplace occupational safety clearance from the HM Government of Gibraltar Health and Safety Inspectorate covering emergency evacuation drills, electrical installation testing, first-aid provision, workstation ergonomic compliance, and employer's liability insurance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar - Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax), Ministry of Finance; official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation; corporate registry: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies, Companies House, https://www.csr.gov.gi
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company (BM_EXEMPTED_CO) must complete the following steps to procure a statutory Gibraltar tax identity: (1) File an external company registration with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 2014 and appoint a Gibraltar resident agent and registered office; (2) Obtain the requisite authorisation from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) for the regulated equity crowdfunding portal activity; (3) Submit a taxpayer registration application to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office (Form IRO/TIN-REG) to obtain a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN), disclosing place of central management and control and the intended Gibraltar permanent establishment; (4) Register with HM Customs Gibraltar for a customs trader code (CTS ID) if any imports/exports of dutiable goods are contemplated; (5) Register for any applicable social/payroll withholding obligations (PAYE and social insurance contributions) if local staff are engaged.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar law does not permit a US-style 'check-the-box' fiscal transparency election. Available elections under the Income Tax Act 2010 (as amended) and related statutes include: (i) seat-of-management election influencing tax residence evidenced by place of central management and control; (ii) group relief and consortium relief elections for qualifying tax groups; (iii) deemed-profit election for approved shipping and insurance activities; (iv) fixed-asset capital allowance elections; and (v) anti-hybrid rule elections aligning with OECD BEPS Action 2. The former Exempt Company and Qualifying Company regimes were abolished with grandfathering only for pre-existing certificates; no new exempt company status is available to a Bermuda Exempted Company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar Consumption Tax/Customs and Excise Import Duty (no VAT or general sales tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable: Gibraltar levies no VAT/GST or general sales tax. Customs import duty/excise applies only to specified dutiable categories (spirits, wine, beer, tobacco products, hydrocarbon oils, and motor vehicles). A customs trader registration is mandatory for any importer of such goods irrespective of turnover; pure financial and crowdfunding intermediary services fall outside the scope of consumption tax, so no economic-turnover registration threshold applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable: Gibraltar does not operate a mandatory real-time e-invoicing clearance regime, fiscal digital stamping, or government API tax-clearance platform. Tax invoices must nonetheless satisfy the record-keeping requirements of the Income Tax Act 2010 and the GFSC conduct-of-business rules, which mandate issuance of proper invoices, retention for at least six years, and electronic submission of customs declarations through the Gibraltar Electronic Customs (GEC) system for any dutiable foreign trade transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Because Gibraltar imposes no VAT/GST, export 'zero-rating' in the EU/UK sense does not apply. Instead, goods physically exported from Gibraltar customs territory are relieved from import/customs consumption duties under the Customs Ordinance, conditional on proof that the goods left Gibraltar, while services rendered to non-resident customers (including crowdfunding technology services and platform access fees) are outside the scope of Gibraltar consumption tax under place-of-supply principles. Eligibility requires documentary evidence of the underlying commercial transaction, direct delivery to the foreign counterparty, and absence of subsequent redelivery into Gibraltar. The Bermuda Exempted Company must be the declared exporter on the customs entry; if it merely acts through a Gibraltar branch, branch records must demonstrate the goods/services left the territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic entry lodged in the Gibraltar Electronic Customs system referencing the CTS trader ID)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (or equivalent multimodal transport document)
Commercial Invoice (itemised; matching declared value, tariff classification, and consignee details)
Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank Credit Advice proving foreign-currency consideration and repatriation of export proceeds
Certified Packing List and Proof of Export (signed dock receipt or carrier certificate of departure)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or incompletely documented export relief claims are audited by HM Customs Gibraltar and the Income Tax Office. Consequences include retrospective claw-back of all duties relieved with interest, confiscation/forfeiture of the goods, monetary penalties up to three times the value of the goods and/or imprisonment under the Customs Ordinance, and, in cases of deliberate tax-abuse connected to understating Gibraltar-source profit, penalties of up to 100% of the tax undercharged plus daily interest under the Income Tax Act 2010. The GFSC may additionally revoke the crowdfunding licence for AML/integrity failings where false export or FX repatriation documentation is used.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (UK central monetary authority; sets monetary policy for GBP and the Gibraltar pound at statutory par) and HM Treasury, which holds reserve exchange-control powers under the Exchange Control Act 1947 (repealed with effect from 1979; no controls currently in force). Gibraltar has no separate central bank; the Gibraltar pound (GIP) is issued at a 1:1 peg with GBP under the Currency Notes Act 1934 and is fully interchangeable with sterling. AML/CTF supervision for banking and payment services in Gibraltar is vested in the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The UK and Gibraltar maintain full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the OECD Codes of Liberalisation; no exchange-control licence, pre-approval, or FX surrender applies to equity subscriptions, crowdfunding client collections, dividend repatriations, or intercompany loans. Profit and capital repatriation from Gibraltar to the Bermuda parent is free of exchange restrictions, subject only to CRS/FATCA reporting and bank-level Bank of England International Transaction Reporting System (ITRS) statistical filings. Crowdfunding investor funds are client moneys and must be safeguarded in a statutory trust or segregated escrow arrangement, not treated as corporate treasury assets.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. The Exchange Control (Repeal) Act 1979 (UK) abolished all surrender and conversion obligations for export and receipt proceeds; no mandatory conversion ratio or statutory timeline exists in the UK or Gibraltar. All crowdfunding ticket proceeds, platform fees, and disbursement returns may be held in any convertible currency and freely hedged; only passive statistical reporting applies via the banking system under the Bank of England ITRS, with direct reporting required if the entity holds foreign-currency balances above applicable de minimis reporting thresholds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. FCA/GFSC-regulated e-money institutions (e.g., Wise, Currencycloud, Modulr) offer rapid multi-currency IBANs, SEPA/FPS connectivity, and automated FX conversion and are compatible with a Gibraltar-licensed crowdfunding portal for operational float only. Legal constraints: an EMI may not grant credit; client money must remain in segregated safeguarding accounts at an authorised credit institution; and most EMIs internally prohibit high-risk merchant sub-classes such as investment-based crowdfunding, requiring prior approved merchant due diligence. The primary client-money escrow must therefore sit with a Tier-1 bank or a dedicated trust/escrow agent, with EMIs used exclusively for fee and operational liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is technically available for UK/Gibraltar licensed corporate structures through video identity verification; however, given the Bermuda Exempted Company wrapper and the High-Risk special-licence crowdfunding classification, most Tier-1 banks mandate a physical due-diligence interview of the designated AML/KYC nominated officer and at least one beneficial-owner director at a London or Gibraltar office. A notarised board resolution, certified passport copies, and the in-life presence of the nominated officer remain the industry norm; a purely remote opening is rarely accepted for escrow accounts holding client funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry red flag: investment-based crowdfunding platform classified as High-Risk_Special_License; investor-money concentration risk and possible FCA COBS 18 applicability
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GFSC crowdfunding licence and any FCA top-up permission; client-money safeguarding policy (statutory trust or third-party escrow); segregation and reconciliation procedures; audited financial statements; complaints handling and 24-hour cooling-off disclosure; prohibition of platform treasury leverage on client balances; fee schedule; internal capital adequacy and wind-down plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structuring red flag: Bermuda Exempted Company with tax-exempt classification and no minimum capital; opacity concerns around ultimate beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Registrar good-standing certificate; certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents; full PSC/beneficial-ownership register with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations for any 25%+ shareholder; notarised identification of all directors; letter of non-trading in Bermuda; confirmation of Gibraltar economic substance with premises, employees, board minutes, and expense records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty red flag: equity issuers on the crowdfunding platform may route funds from sanctioned, embargoed, or politically exposed persons; AML risk of reverse on-boarding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform-level KYC/KYB policy incorporating sanctions screening against OFSI, EU, UK, UN, and OFAC lists; geo-blocking of prohibited jurisdictions; transaction-monitoring and negative-news screening; enhanced due-diligence standards for PEPs; contractual warranties from issuers; escrow account designated solely for investor funds; record-retention policy of at least five years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory status red flag: doubt over licence scope between Gibraltar and United Kingdom passporting, plus absence of statutory authorisation for payment services if the portal touches client funds directly
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed legal opinion from a Gibraltar-licensed law firm under the Gibraltar Financial Services Act 2019; written confirmation that the platform operates as an investment intermediary, not a payment institution; evidence that payment initiation is delegated to an FCA-authorised or GFSC-authorised payment/e-money institution; SWIFT/SEPA service agreements with the clearing bank; HM Treasury and FCA notification correspondence, where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from the Bermuda parent to the Gibraltar operating treasury are routed by SWIFT MT103; GBP settlements clear over CHAPS (same-day, above £1M) or Faster Payments (below £1M), with EUR finality over TARGET2/SEPA. Remittance information must state the purpose as a direct-investment equity contribution 'P.711 - Equity other than investment fund shares' (BPM6 financial-account code) and the sending bank must include the supporting board resolution, certificate of incumbency, and latest audited financial statements, which are provided to the receiving bank's relationship manager before crediting. For USD wires, intermediate correspondent routing (e.g., Barclays or HSBC New York CHIPS branch) is required; the receiving bank must be pre-notified to avoid AML pends.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements to portfolio companies are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR, Faster Payments for GBP (subject to counterparty limits and risk thresholds), and SWIFT MT103 for USD and non-SEPA currencies; all settlements are correspondent-bank cleared and reportable under the Bank of England ITRS. A commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700) is permissible only where the crowdfunding portal pre-finances trade-backed instruments and must be supported by confirmed LC issuers; standard escrow releases require dual signature from the compliance officer and an independent escrow agent; no crypto rail or unregulated value-transfer mechanism may be used.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/GBP, USD/GBP) with tenors up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
Vanilla FX Call/Put Options and Collar Structures on major convertible pairs
FX Swaps and Cross-Currency Swaps for balance-sheet hedging of intercompany loans
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for exotic currencies only where no deliverable market exists; expressly prohibited for GBP/EUR/USD G10 pairs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts BMD 250 per month or part (max BMD 1,000); continued default leads to administrative strike-off and potential winding up.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Return (Form 100) for Foreign Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of registration in Gibraltar + 42 calendar days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalties escalate with delay: GBP 50 (late), GBP 200 (3-6 months), GBP 300 (6-12 months), GBP 500 (over 12 months); persistent non-filing results in court order or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GFSC Equity Crowdfunding Portal Annual Licence Renewal and Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 December each calendar year (per licence condition)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment or non-submission may result in licence suspension or revocation, financial penalties up to GBP 1,000,000 for unauthorised regulated activity, and personal liability of directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all GFSC-licensed equity crowdfunding portals regardless of size; otherwise under Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, audit is required if any two of the following exceed: turnover GBP 10.2M, balance-sheet total GBP 5.1M, average employees 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Gibraltar; Bermuda legal framework permits IFRS or US GAAP, but GFSC license requires IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Bermuda maintains a standing register of beneficial owners at the registered office, updated on any trigger event; no annual confirmation filing. Gibraltar requires UBO particulars to be annually confirmed via the Form 100 annual return and updated within 14 days of any shareholding transfer or beneficial ownership change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (Bermuda and Gibraltar)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,000–6,000 (combined Bermuda and Gibraltar registered office and corporate agent services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000–30,000 (GFSC-regulated audit under IFRS, varies with transaction volume)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Flat 12.5% CIT on assessable profits; no VAT; no capital gains tax on share disposals (only Gibraltar land/buildings gains taxable); no Gibraltar withholding on distributions; Bermuda Exempted Co tax exemption certificate does not extend to Gibraltar-source activities. Trading losses can be carried forward indefinitely (no carry-back); no statutory tax holidays, but qualifying foreign tax credits and unilateral relief are available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form CIT (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via GRIS (Gibraltar Revenue Integrated System) at gris.gibraltar.gov.gi; paper dual-filing accepted only on Commissioner's written consent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be delivered within 12 months of the end of the accounting period. Example: 31 December 2024 year-end is due on 31 December 2025. Self-assessed tax is payable by the filing deadline; interest accrues at 7% per annum on late payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Gibraltar tax reference (TRN), registered company number, registered office address in Gibraltar, date of incorporation, country of incorporation (Bermuda), and place of central management and control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident Bermuda Exempted Co carrying on a trade in Gibraltar must enter its foreign company registration number under the Gibraltar Companies (Overseas Companies) Act and identify the Gibraltar agent; tax reference is issued by the Commissioner before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the accounting period covered by the return; must match the audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same period as the Bermuda statutory accounts; if the Bermuda entity prepares accounts to a different date, prepare separate Gibraltar branch accounts and reconcile in Box 44.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross trading income from the equity crowdfunding platform (arrangement fees, success fees, platform fees, escrow interest), rent, royalties, dividends, interest, and other income; includes Gibraltar-source income of non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: include only Gibraltar-source income (fees earned from Gibraltar investors or issuers physically present in Gibraltar). Resident: include worldwide income. Escrow interest is taxable even if credited to a segregated client account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Wholly and exclusively incurred expenses: salaries, regulatory licence fees (GFSC), AML compliance costs, technology hosting, legal/professional fees, rent, and capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Branch expenses must be apportioned to the Gibraltar permanent establishment using arm's length transfer pricing; Bermuda head-office general overheads are deductible only to the extent attributable to the Gibraltar branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible items: client entertainment, fines, penalties, non-wholly-and-exclusively expenses, depreciated accounting depreciation, and transfer pricing upward adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest charged by the Bermuda parent to the Gibraltar operation is deductible only if it satisfies the arm's length principle and the relevant borrowing is used for bona fide commercial purposes; excessive related-party charges must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted trading profit after add-backs and deductions, capital allowances, trading losses brought forward claimed, relevant chargeable income, taxable profits at 12.5%, and any non-excluded charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carry forward Bermuda tax losses is not permitted; only losses arising in the Gibraltar trade or overseas trade of a Gibraltar-resident company may be carried forward under the Income Tax Act. Compute tax at 12.5% on the taxable profits attributable to Gibraltar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Double taxation relief: foreign tax credit for withholding taxes suffered on foreign-source income, unilateral relief, and treaty credits under the UK-Gibraltar DTA 2019.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Gibraltar Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) and the foreign tax voucher/assessment; credit is limited to the lower of foreign tax paid and the Gibraltar 12.5% effective rate on the same income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-assessed tax liability, tax paid by instalments or on account, balance due or refund claimed; bank details for refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents without a Gibraltar bank account must pay via cleared wire transfer to the Income Tax Office collection account; the balance is payable by the statutory deadline to avoid 7% p.a. interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of a director or company secretary, name, position, date, and confirmation that the return is complete and accurate to the best of knowledge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Bermuda Exempted Co's designated Gibraltar representative may sign if expressly authorised; false declaration triggers personal liability of the subscribing officer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: initial penalty GIP 100; daily default GIP 60 for up to 90 days; further tax-geared penalty GIP 100–900 if failure continues beyond 6 months. Inaccurate return: up to 100% of understated tax (reasonable care), 150% for deliberate concealment. Late payment interest: 7% per annum. Criminal prosecution possible for persistent non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% domestic dividend withholding tax; no Gibraltar withholding is levied on distributions to shareholders, whether resident or non-resident.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Domestic WHT is nil, so treaty relief for Gibraltar-source dividends is generally unnecessary. For outbound treaty protection, the Gibraltar-resident company applies to the Income Tax Office for a Certificate of Tax Residence (Form TRC); the TRC is then used to claim credit or exemption in the source state. The only comprehensive DTA is the UK–Gibraltar Double Taxation Agreement (signed May 2019, effective 1 January 2020), which allocates taxing rights and provides foreign tax credit mechanism; other jurisdictions are covered by TIEAs. Foreign tax credits are claimed on Form CIT Part 7.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic rates for non-residents: interest 0%; royalties 0%. Under the UK–Gibraltar DTA, interest and royalties remain taxable only in the beneficial owner's state of residence (0% source WHT). No non-resident withholding return is required in Gibraltar.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory de minimis threshold is published in Gibraltar; the Commissioner can require a Transfer Pricing Report on a risk basis for any controlled transaction. Practically, maintain Local File where annual controlled turnover exceeds GIP 1,000,000 or where related-party service fees exceed GIP 250,000. Master File and CbC Report apply to MNE groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 (approx. GIP 634,000,000) in the prior fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Yes. Gibraltar Economic Substance (Companies and Partnerships) Regulations 2021 apply. A crowdfunding portal falls within 'financing and leasing' / 'fund management' as a relevant activity. The entity must demonstrate in Gibraltar: (1) direction and management independence, (2) core income-generating activities (CIGA) physically performed in Gibraltar, (3) adequate premises, (4) qualified full-time employees, and (5) operating expenditure proportionate to income. Annual ESR report filing is mandatory; the low-tax exempt status of the Bermuda parent does not exempt the Gibraltar operation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly or recklessly submitting a false Form CIT, suppressing Gibraltar-source crowdfunding fees, fabricating deductible expenses, or destroying records to reduce the 12.5% CIT charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2010: civil penalty up to 150% of the evaded tax; criminal conviction on indictment: unlimited fine and imprisonment up to 7 years; on summary conviction: fine up to GIP 50,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years. Interest at 7% p.a. runs from the date tax should have been paid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any director, manager, or company secretary who 'knowingly causes, permits, or contributes' to the false return is jointly and severally liable for the company's tax penalty; subject to disqualification under the Company Directors Disqualification Act (Gibraltar) for up to 15 years; civil restitution orders and travel restraint orders may be issued to prevent departure from Gibraltar pending recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming Gibraltar tax residence or operating the crowdfunding licence without real presence: no physical office, no full-time employees in Gibraltar, board meetings held entirely abroad, or booking all revenues through the Bermuda parent while performing CIGA in Gibraltar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Economic Substance Regulations 2021: financial penalty up to GIP 50,000 per failure plus daily default penalties up to GIP 1,000; the Commissioner may reclassify the entity as non-resident and assess 12.5% on all Gibraltar-source income without relief; automatic exchange of substance information with UK HMRC and EU member states under DAC6/CBCR frameworks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors' enabling of substance failure can result in personal penalties up to GIP 50,000 and disqualification; if the company becomes insolvent due to penalties, directors may face wrongful trading liability under Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 and contribution orders for the full penalty amount.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an equity crowdfunding portal under ISIC 6499 without the requisite Financial Services Commission (GFSC) licence under the Financial Services Act 2019, or failing to implement Anti-Money Laundering obligations: missing customer due diligence, not filing Suspicious Activity Reports, handling investor funds outside the authorised escrow bank, or facilitating unregulated crowd-investing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed activity: fine up to GIP 100,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years; each day of operation is a separate offence. AML failure under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2011 (as amended) and AML/CFT Regulations: substantial regulatory fines up to GIP 250,000 per breach; personal criminal liability for money laundering carries imprisonment up to 14 years and unlimited fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) are personally criminally liable for deliberate AML failures; travel bans and asset freezing orders under the Proceeds of Crime Act may be imposed; compensation orders in favour of defrauded investors are made directly against the directors' personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Extracting profits to the Bermuda parent via excessive management fees, artificial royalty payments, non-arm's length loan interest, or dividend payments disguised as loan repayments, without supporting economic substance or documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax re-characterisation under Income Tax Act 2010 s.24A: the Commissioner substitutes the arm's length consideration, disallows the deduction, and assesses additional 12.5% CIT plus interest; penalty for negligent transfer pricing up to 100% of the additional tax; for deliberate transfer pricing concealment, up to 150%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the CIT return knowing the transfer pricing adjustments were not arm's length are personally liable for the accuracy penalty; cross-border tax avoidance arrangements may trigger HMRC/Gibraltar anti-abuse rulings and director disqualification; failure to maintain TP documentation shifts burden of proof to the taxpayer and exposes directors to personal examination under oath.
